vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded JWT_SECRET in Repository
vulnerabilities.description: JWT_SECRET is hardcoded in .env file. While .env is in .gitignore, if ever committed, these secrets are permanently compromised. All JWT tokens signed with this secret are now at risk.
vulnerabilities.impact: Session hijacking, account takeover, privilege escalation

vulnerabilities.title: Exposed Reddit OAuth Credentials
vulnerabilities.description: REDDIT_CLIENT_ID and REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET are hardcoded in .env. These credentials can be used to impersonate the application to Reddit's API.
vulnerabilities.impact: Unauthorized access to Reddit API, potential data exfiltration, API quota exhaustion

vulnerabilities.title: Exposed Anthropic API Key
vulnerabilities.description: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is hardcoded in .env. This key allows anyone to make API calls on behalf of the application, consuming credits and accessing model services.
vulnerabilities.impact: Unauthorized API usage, credit card fraud, quota exhaustion

vulnerabilities.title: Unauthenticated Health Endpoint Information Disclosure
vulnerabilities.description: The /health endpoint is publicly accessible (no requireAuth) and exposes: LLM_PROVIDER, error messages from external services, and LLM responses. An attacker can fingerprint the system and gather intelligence about the infrastructure.
vulnerabilities.code_snippet: app.get('/health', async () => { ... return { llm: { provider: process.env['LLM_PROVIDER'], error: error.message } } })
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure, reconnaissance for further attacks

vulnerabilities.title: Health Endpoint Resource Exhaustion (DoS)
vulnerabilities.description: The /health endpoint makes a real LLM API call without rate limiting. An attacker can spam this endpoint to exhaust API credits and cause denial of service.
vulnerabilities.code_snippet: app.get('/health', async () => { const llmResponse = await callLLM('Say LLM is working...');
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of service, financial loss from API usage

vulnerabilities.title: Database URL Logging to Console
vulnerabilities.description: console.log(process.env.DATABASE_URL) exposes database credentials. If logs are captured, stored, or exposed, attackers gain direct database access with full credentials.
vulnerabilities.impact: Direct database access, data breach, data manipulation

vulnerabilities.title: JWT Cookie Not Signed
vulnerabilities.description: The access_token cookie is created with { signed: false }, meaning the cookie value is not cryptographically signed. While the JWT itself is signed, the cookie is vulnerable to tampering at the transport layer.
vulnerabilities.impact: Cookie tampering, though JWT signature still provides some protection

vulnerabilities.title: Excessive Error Detail Leakage
vulnerabilities.description: The global error handler returns full error.validation details and error.message to clients. This can leak information about database structure, field names, and system internals.
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure for reconnaissance and exploitation

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficient CORS Configuration Validation
vulnerabilities.description: CORS origin uses process.env['WEB_URL'] directly without validation or URL parsing. While it's an environment variable (not user input), misconfiguration could enable CSRF attacks.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential CSRF attacks if WEB_URL is misconfigured

vulnerabilities.title: Environment Variable Error Messages Leak Expectations
vulnerabilities.description: The requireEnv function throws errors listing expected variable names. An attacker can use this to understand the system's dependencies and identify missing configurations.
vulnerabilities.code_snippet: throw new Error(`Missing required environment variable: ${key}`)

vulnerabilities.title: Global Rate Limit May Be Insufficient
vulnerabilities.description: 100 requests per minute applied globally to all endpoints. This is a single rate limit for the entire API with no per-endpoint or per-user granularity. Critical endpoints might need stricter limits.
vulnerabilities.impact: Abuse of expensive endpoints (e.g., /health calling LLM)

vulnerabilities.title: Timing Attack Vulnerability in Credential Verification
vulnerabilities.description: The verifyCredentials function may be vulnerable to timing attacks. If the bcrypt comparison timing differs based on password existence, an attacker could enumerate valid usernames.
vulnerabilities.code_snippet: const [user] = await db.select().from(users).where(...); if (!user) throw new Error('INVALID_CREDENTIALS'); const valid = await bcrypt.compare(...);
vulnerabilities.impact: User enumeration, but impact is mitigated by generic error message

vulnerabilities.title: Debug Logging Enabled in Development
vulnerabilities.description: Development mode logs at 'info' level with pino-pretty. While useful for debugging, ensure sensitive data isn't logged in development environments that might be accessible.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential credential leakage in development logs

summary.overall_assessment: The application has significant security vulnerabilities, primarily around exposed secrets and unauthenticated endpoints that leak information or enable resource exhaustion. While core database queries are protected via Drizzle ORM parameterization, secret management and API endpoint security require immediate attention.

details: Generate new JWT_SECRET and JWT_REFRESH_SECRET using cryptographically secure random generation
Rotate REDDIT_CLIENT_ID and REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET through Reddit's developer portal
Regenerate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY through Anthropic's dashboard
If these secrets were ever committed to git, treat as permanently compromised
Either add { preHandler: [requireAuth] } to protect the endpoint
Or replace with a simple status-only response that doesn't call external APIs
Remove LLM_PROVIDER and error details from response
recommendations.example: app.get('/health', async () => ({ status: 'ok', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() }))

details: Delete packages/api/check-env.ts if not in use
If needed for debugging, ensure it's only callable locally and never exposed via HTTP
Change fastifyJwt registration to: cookie: { cookieName: 'access_token', signed: true }
Ensure the same jwtSecret is used for signing
Add per-endpoint rate limits (stricter for /health and auth endpoints)
Implement per-user rate limiting for authenticated endpoints
Consider per-IP rate limiting for public endpoints
Install @fastify/helmet and register it
Enable CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS
Configure based on your security requirements
Never return validation details or raw error messages to clients
Return generic error messages: 'Validation failed' instead of field-specific details
Log detailed errors server-side only
Use environment variables for ALL secrets (already doing this - good!)
Implement secret versioning in your secret management system
Add alerts for when secrets are accessed via logs
Consider using AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, or similar

recommendations.action: Add input sanitization for competitive advantage
details: While Zod validates URL format, consider additional sanitization
Ensure URLs don't contain javascript: protocols or other XSS vectors

positive_findings: ✅ Passwords are properly hashed with bcryptjs (12 salt rounds)
✅ Database queries use Drizzle ORM with parameterized queries - no SQL injection risk
✅ All API routes have proper authentication checks via requireAuth
✅ Authorization is properly scoped to user's workspace
✅ All sensitive secrets are read from environment variables (not hardcoded in code)
✅ GitHub safe helper properly uses execFileSync to prevent shell injection
✅ Cookie security flags are set (httpOnly, sameSite)
test_recommendations: Penetration test the /health endpoint for DoS vulnerability
Test for timing attacks in credential verification
Verify rate limiting is working correctly
Test CORS configuration with different origins
Check logs don't expose sensitive information
Verify database URL isn't accessible via error messages
